lines.say: Cartier rebuilt a lost two thousand nine hundred thirty diamond necklace.

lines.text: In 1928, the Maharaja of Patiala ordered a Cartier necklace.
lines.say: In nineteen twenty-eight, the Maharaja of Patiala ordered a Cartier necklace.

lines.text: It held 2,930 diamonds, set in platinum.
lines.say: It held two thousand nine hundred thirty diamonds, set in platinum.

lines.text: Its center was a pale yellow diamond of about 234 carats.
lines.say: Its center was a pale yellow diamond of about two hundred thirty-four carats.

lines.text: Around 1948, it was reported missing from the royal treasury,
lines.say: Around nineteen forty-eight, it was reported missing from the royal treasury,

lines.text: In 1982 the big diamond alone turned up at a Geneva auction.
lines.say: In nineteen eighty-two the big diamond alone turned up at a Geneva auction.

lines.text: In 1998, its platinum frame turned up in a London shop.
lines.say: In nineteen ninety-eight, its platinum frame turned up in a London shop.

lines.text: Cartier bought it and rebuilt it by 2002,
lines.say: Cartier bought it and rebuilt it by two thousand two,

lines.text: using stand-ins, such as zirconia and topaz, for the lost stones.
In 2025, it was shown at the V&A in London.

post.caption: Cartier made the Patiala Necklace in 1928 with 2,930 diamonds. It went missing around 1948, and in 1998 its platinum frame turned up in a London shop. Cartier bought it and rebuilt it with stand-in stones. It was shown at the V&A in 2025.
